# Answer: generator-shortcuts

## Strongest plausible canonical-fitting shortcut

**Connect only the longest aligned pair of equal nonzero colors, ignoring which
color it is.** Paint cyan only between that one pair.

This is stronger and more plausible than “connect every repeated color” because
it still changes only one object, just like the intended rule. It fits all five
canonical demonstrations: in each one, the magenta pair is longer than the only
repeated decoration pair, whose two cells are adjacent.

## Exact disagreement case

Generated by version `4.0.0` with:

- seed: `0`
- sample index: `2` (`short_separated` role)
- difficulty: `easy`

Input:

```text
00010001
00000000
00000000
00060600
00000000
00000000
00000000
00000000
```

The magenta endpoints are distance 2 apart, with one zero between them. The two
color-1 decorations are distance 4 apart.

Intended output — select magenta and fill its strict interior:

```text
00010001
00000000
00000000
00068600
00000000
00000000
00000000
00000000
```

Rival output — select the longer color-1 pair instead:

```text
00018881
00000000
00000000
00060600
00000000
00000000
00000000
00000000
```

## How it was checked

The executable rival was run against normalized canonical pairs and matched
5/5. The exact input above was passed to the intended Python semantic mirror and
the rival; their outputs differ as shown. The after rule-smoke check independently
established 120/120 agreement between the Python mirror and the selected Racket
authority, with zero crashes. The semantic gate also verified the rival claim
on 60 sampled witness cases.

## Does the generator emit such cases?

Yes, deterministically in every default four-sample curriculum cycle at the
`short_separated` residue. A focused probe over 100 seeds and 16 sample indices
per band found 400 such cases in each of easy, medium, and hard. In all
1,200/1,200 cases the irrelevant pair was strictly longer than the magenta pair,
and the rival disagreed with the intended rule.
